description: A reified 'observationOriginActivity' relation: an evidence node and the activity at the origin of the data it rests on (subject = evidence, object = a study or a protocol). Maps to the MIRA schema's observationOriginActivity slot (github.com/MIRA-science/schema, mira.yaml on main: slot_uri mira:observationOriginActivity, title 'Observation origin process', 'An experiment or study at the origin of the data on which the observation is based', domain Evidence, range Activity; MIRA's Study and Protocol both mix in Activity, so RRGI's study and protocol are the concrete objects). One of MIRA's four evidence links, added to RRGI on 2026-10-03. Where it overlaps RRGI's provenance spine (study → grounds → evidence, the same fact read from the study's side), extractors keep writing grounds; this relation is accepted and shown whenever someone uses it. MIRA notes upstream that, when sourceDocument is also given, the origin activity should be one the source document describes (a property chain it deliberately does not assert). MIRA marks observationBase's range as provisional: mira.yaml's own comment on it reads "That range is very, very provisional. could also involve schema:DigitalDocument , schema:Dataset", so this shape may change when MIRA settles it. (The provisional note belongs to observationBase, the sibling evidence link; it is repeated on each of MIRA's four evidence links here so their provisional status is visible wherever one is used.) RRGI's intentional divergence (matching supports): subject/object are dual-addressed via com.atproto.repo.strongRef (uri + cid) instead of a bare at-uri, so the edge pins exact content versions and cannot rot. NOTE: no upstream atproto lexicon exists for this type yet; authored ahead of upstream from the MIRA schema, intended to be proposed back.

subject.description: Dual-addressed reference (URI + CID) to the evidence (the observation). RRGI divergence from upstream's bare at-uri: com.atproto.repo.strongRef requires both uri and cid, so the CID is mandatory.

object.description: Dual-addressed reference (URI + CID) to the activity at the origin of its data (a study or a protocol). See subject: RRGI divergence, CID mandatory.

description.description: Optional elaboration: how the study or protocol produced the data the evidence rests on.
